neighbours.label: discovering that something is gone: a person or object found missing, vanished or empty, as against the same scene with it still there
fire: When the guards checked the vault at dawn, the gold bars were gone.
I reached into my pocket and realised my keys were missing.
By the time the police arrived, the stolen car was gone from the lot.
She lifted the lid of the cookie jar and found it empty again.
After the storm, three of the boats in the harbour were missing.
He woke up in the hotel room to find his roommate gone and the door open.
The archaeologists opened the coffin and discovered it was empty.
Returning from lunch, the clerk saw that the cash box was gone.
quiet: When the guards checked the vault at dawn, the gold bars were safe.
I reached into my pocket and pulled out my keys.
By the time the police arrived, the stolen car was parked in the lot.
She lifted the lid of the cookie jar and took out a biscuit.
After the storm, three of the boats in the harbour were damaged.
He woke up in the hotel room to find his roommate asleep and the door locked.
The archaeologists opened the coffin and discovered a gold mask.
Returning from lunch, the clerk counted the money in the cash box.

predictions: fire 0.5-1.0 on ' gone', ' missing', ' empty'; same scenes with the thing present below 0.15
notes: Card: ' gone' x11, ' missing' x4, ' empty' x3 ('belongings were gone', 'tomb... empty', 'wakes up to find her gone'). Probe: 'all our food were gone' 1.099, 'found it empty' 0.769, 'wallet was missing' 0.734; 'still there' 0.119, 'found her grandmother's ring' 0.031; 'nowhere to be seen' only 0.169, 'summer has gone quickly' 0.167, so fire items use gone/missing/empty in the vanished sense.
